models.label: ESP32 DevKit (30-pin)
models.description: DOIT ESP32 DevKit V1 and its 30-pin clones.

reset.label: a button between GPIO 19 (D19) and GND

notes: Header labels like D13 mean GPIO 13.

models.label: ESP32 DevKit (38-pin)

reset.label: a button between GPIO 19 and GND

notes: The extra pins on this board (GPIO 0 and 6–11) are BOOT and the flash chip's: never wire them.

models.label: ESP32-C3 Super Mini
models.description: The thumb-sized ESP32-C3 board with USB-C.
notes: Some Super Mini boards need BOOT held while plugging in before they can be flashed.
I2C here is on GPIO 5 (SDA) and 6 (SCL): GPIO 8 and 9, often printed as SDA/SCL, are this board's LED and BOOT button.

models.label: ESP32-S3 DevKitC-1
models.description: Espressif's ESP32-S3 DevKitC-1 (v1.0) and most clones: RGB LED on GPIO 48.
notes: Plug it in by the USB port labelled UART (the other is the chip's own USB).
If its RGB LED stays dark while the board runs, it's a v1.1 board: pick ESP32-S3 DevKitC-1 v1.1.

models.label: ESP32-S3 DevKitC-1 v1.1
models.description: The v1.1 revision, with its RGB LED moved to GPIO 38.
notes: Plug it in by the USB port labelled UART (the other is the chip's own USB).
